title: MASQ: The Multi-Agent System Questionnaire
description: We introduce the multi-agent system questionnaire (MASQ), a three-stage screening framework that connects system design choices to plausible miscoordination risks and their observable manifestations. Stage 3 guides researchers in examining MAS execution traces for evidence of anticipated and unanticipated miscoordination.

paper.title: MASQ: The Multi-Agent System Questionnaire
paper.authors: Nils Kiele, Niki Mehri, Aaron Arellano, Samira Ebrahimi Kahou

example_outputs.title: Default inputs
example_outputs.summary: An LLM filling in MASQ for ChatDev anticipated 8 of 14 failure modes, the same count as the authors. In a small ChatDev-style chain, 3 of 5 tasks declared done failed hidden tests. Stage 2 ratings are an LLM applying the paper's rule, not the authors' labels. Five traces give coarse rates.

inputs.label: System preset
inputs.description: chatdev (the paper's ChatDev description; overlaid on Table 2) or groupchat (a hypothetical research-assistant group chat written for this runbook)

inputs.label: Your system
inputs.description: Paste a description of your multi-agent system (roles, who talks to whom, how they communicate, termination and verification, memory). Overrides the preset

inputs.label: Run Stage 3
inputs.description: Run the mini chat chain and annotate its traces (false = Stages 1–2 only, ~10 s)

inputs.label: Traces
inputs.description: Number of Stage-3 traces (2–6; one coding task each)

inputs.label: Mini-MAS verification
inputs.description: prompt (tester reads the code, like ChatDev's role-prompted tester) or tests (tester's asserts are actually executed)

inputs.label: Mini-MAS memory
inputs.description: drop (only the final artefact passes between phases, like ChatDev) or shared (full history visible)

inputs.label: Review rounds
inputs.description: Hard cap on reviewer ⇄ programmer rounds (1–3)

inputs.label: Annotator size
inputs.description: small (Claude Haiku) or large (Claude Sonnet) for the MAST trace annotation
